reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is a strong outing from Guy Ritchie, one his fans and others should go back and see for the first time or get back to so they can see more of the details and art on display here.
reviews.author: Emilie Black

reviews.text: The filmmaker plows forward utterly unburdened by even the slightest hint of substance. It’s admirable, really. This movie makes a trifle look like a T-bone steak.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A ceaselessly satisfying tiki-bar timewaster that tells a common story often punctuated by innovative idiosyncrasies like a spy pausing a chase to savor a sandwich that looks very tasty or a cohort losing herself, however briefly, to a pop song's rhythms.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: There is a smugness to the whole proceeding that sometimes shows itself in the self-indulgent style and in Ritchie’s infatuation with how good his actors look. But there is also an undeniable allure.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A sequel would be welcomed with opened arms and a reserved seat by this critic.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's first film since 2011 is a stylish and jovial spy caper.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: It may be as deep as a puddle, but splashing around hasn't been this enjoyable in a while.
reviews.author: Tony Black

reviews.text: Although it doesn't completely accomplish its mission, The Man From U.N.C.L.E. fits in with the pack as a lighthearted, charming, and stylish take on the spy genre.
reviews.author: Rudie Obias

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's attempt at a James Bond movie is action-packed, funny and utterly charming.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: As evidence of Guy Ritchie's new position as one of the better genre directors around, it's a diverting confection and worth a visit.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: A rollicking spy caper, full of attractive people looking fabulous and exotic locations where you wish you were.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is a slick and stylish spy movie ... an entertaining diversion for an afternoon.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: It was almost a great movie.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Some of it was really fun.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Cavill, as well as Armie Hammer and the delicious Alicia Vikander, play from the beginning the difficult game of engaging the audience. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: Ritchie's sophisticated, multi-character drama says the world will be saved with wit, invention, and complex cooperation. Which is why it feels dated, and is struggling at the box office.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: What's surprising isn't just the de-mothballing of a concept no one was missing; it's that The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is somehow pretty darn good.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A blockbuster film that has an identity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: In short, The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is good action cinema with filtered humor, of own art and with well entertained moments. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Ritchie seems to distrust the material he has to work with and falls into irrelevant assembly games in which he tries to surprise the viewer without intriguing them first. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: Round for Ritchie - he has two spies for the price of one ... and without paying tolls for 007 -, his triumphant smile turns out to be contagious during the development of The Man From U.N.C.L.E. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manuel Piñón

reviews.text: The dialogue is the movie's biggest problem. The overwhelming reaction I had immediately after leaving was, "Guy Ritchie thinks his writing is much funnier than it is."
reviews.author: Lesley Coffin

reviews.text: It's not a great film, but the performances are all fun, and Guy Ritchie's direction is one of the most enjoyable and luxurious deployments of pure style I've seen in a long time.
reviews.author: Jeff Spross

reviews.text: There are worse things to watch on the big screen this August, but unless you're in the mood for a throwaway movie with little to remember beyond its gorgeous visuals, there's still no compelling reason to cast one's lot with this team.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: It succeeds admirably on its own terms - more so, I think, than his two Sherlock Holmes films - and while it never really transcends pastiche, its ambitions don't lie in that direction.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The high-octane thrill of Guy Ritchie's Sherlock films has been replaced by boring, hot guys suavely saving the world in this remake of the 60s TV show.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Although The Man from U.N.C.L.E. doesn't break any new ground and might not be everyone's mission of choice, it's stylish, fun, and an entertaining enough entry in a crowded lineup of spy-thriller fare.
reviews.author: Beth McDonough

reviews.text: Ritchie has tried to make a sleek and smart period spy caper, but The Man From U.N.C.L.E. falls short of any of its intended opposition. Looks great, but feels wrong.
reviews.author: Bertie Archer

reviews.text: A highly stylized and entertaining spy film worth seeing.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: I had a good time watching this movie despite the terrible action and directing choices.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The story, such as it is, is entirely secondary to the parade of stylish outfits and equally stylish action set-pieces.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: As a late-summer action romp, The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is easy-peasy viewing. It's fast, it's fun, and it's brimming with attitude.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: The film is very fun and maintains a level of sobriety about its humor. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: Director Guy Ritchie crafts a slick, enjoyable retro-funky barrage of musical-action set pieces.
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: The movie glossily captures the vibe of the era with flair.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Suffers from trying too hard to be cool -- the adaptation falls flat.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: THE MAN FROM U.N.C.L.E. Has The Style But Refuses To Break A Sweat
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: It delivers laughs that are actually funny. And it's got action sequences that are thrilling without being overdone.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: The outlandishness of U.N.C.L.E. is truly true to form in the tradition of the funky and frenetic fables that Ritchie loves to spin at will. Both Cavill and Hammer seem to get inspiration out of their dressy roles as the inventive spies
reviews.author: Frank Ochieng

reviews.text: Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer's chemistry is worth it alone, but the added 60s flair just sweetens the deal.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Like the campy Euro-centric spy films of 50 years ago it harkens back to, it's entertaining and enjoyable precisely because of its unabashedly superficial nature.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Its fifty years ago and unfamiliar and worlds away from the one we inhabit now. But it's just as intense. Ritchie dials up the tension in each successive sequence the way he did it so well in his earlier pictures and it is excruciating at certain points.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: I may not remember seeing The Man from U.N.C.L.E. at the end of the year because it is not bringing anything especially inventive to the screen.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: A jet-setting game of cat and mouse that suits naptime more than movie time.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: It's a good-looking film and the three leads hold our attention.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Ritchie's movie is posing from the off. As such, this Man from U.N.C.L.E is one very poor relation.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: The high-energy feature captures much of the spirit of the original, especially in the two leads--Henry Cavill as Solo and Armie Hammer as Kuryakin...
reviews.author: Bill Brioux

reviews.text: How desperately, crashingly bored and short of ideas Ritchie must be to write an entire scene about Paco Rabanne. The results are curiously sexless.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: The good news is that Guy Ritchie injects the film with enough ingenuity so as not to insult his viewers...[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Fans of the original show will probably get more mileage even though this is probably nothing like it barring the actual characters
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: It's actually quite remarkable just how entertaining and compelling The Man from U.N.C.L.E. remains for much of its running time...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Where the TV show's Robert Vaughn and David McCallum enjoyed an effortlessly bickering, bantering rapport, Cavill and Armie Hammer's Kuryakin look as if they've just been crated to the set by FedEx and have never met before.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: The acting, the humour, the script... this is a film that falls miserably short right across the board.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Too bad that U.N.C.L.E. can't even muster enough thrills for a final life-jolting pop. Instead, Ritchie and the movie strike a pose and leave us waiting and wanting.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Much of the action in UNCLE is rendered incoherent by Ritchie's chop-shop action direction. Ritchie has a distinctive style, but like Zack Snyder and Michael Bay he has a tendency to overplay his talents.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is thrilling in a way few action movies are, and certainly far more thrilling than anything Ritchie has directed up until this point.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie should moonlight as a fashion stylist.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: What ought to pop and fizz simply plops along. If Mr. Ritchie was aiming for sleekness and suavity, what he ends up with is a stagnant muddle.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: This is a summer popcorn movie, certainly, but an expertly crafted one, full of thrills and big laughs.
reviews.author: Danielle Riendeau

reviews.text: Though the buddy cop aesthetic is old hat, Cavil and Hammer keep the film afloat...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: I enjoyed The Man from U.N.C.L.E well enough, and I suspect you will, too.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: It all ends up sounding a bit like The Matrix's Agent Smith doing Roger Moore doing James Bond.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer are fine. They're FINE. They're maddeningly, generically fine.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: The plot is disposable at best... but [Guy] Ritchie goes all out in reviving the Cold War sixties spy movie style and attitude, recalling Connery's Bond movies with tongue firmly in cheek.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: This becomes a film feels like a cover version of a cover version. One that neither sends up old spy cinema nor adds much to it with its trans-Euro express of a plot.
reviews.author: Russell Baillie

reviews.text: A gigantic leap forward for the mannequin acting community.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Sophisticated and slick, Ritchie's film is far more appealing than his take on Sherlock. ... The dialogue is crisp and as elegant as the film's fashions, production design and Italian locations.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is Ritchie's first film in almost four years and if he is ever to be considered an auteur, which his initial rise promised, he needs to do something spectacular and soon.
reviews.author: Marija Djurovic

reviews.text: The Man Fr om U.N.C.L.E. is pulpy and fluffy, but knows it is, and never sacrifices its joie de vivre. I'd like to see this cast together again - it'd probably be a lot of fun.
reviews.author: Martin Roberts

reviews.text: Positively in love with the deep-down roots of the genre and the era that spawned them.
reviews.author: Nathan Bartlebaugh

reviews.text: Ritchie and company have turned The Man from U.N.C.L.E. into a highly entertaining, immeasurably stylish, and thoroughly enjoyable movie.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Slick, sexy and stylish... U.N.C.L.E. is A-O.K.
reviews.author: Alex Zane

reviews.text: With significant performance and plotting issues, the film ends up being about as fun as you could expect and just a little bit more.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: There's a bit of a plot twist but it has little impact because by the time it arrives, you just don't care about the characters. Instead, we have to settle for a few clever lines of dialogue, a lovely aesthetic and moderate entertainment value,
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: The movie is packed with action, wit and charm, with director Ritchie sticking to the roots of the original 60s series.
reviews.author: Georgia Morgan

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is not the action movie of the summer -- but it's the one I enjoyed the most.
reviews.author: Alex Abad-Santos

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is tongue in cheek. But still, it's slow going. For a Guy Ritchie movie, that may be the saddest thing to say.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: The re-invention might have been better as straight-up thriller. More story and less comedy fails would have helped.
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: The main problem with The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is its tone. We can't take this stuff seriously, yet Ritchie misses all sorts of opportunities to make the movie fun. The result isn't particularly satisfying as either adventure or comedy.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is a massive disappointment that flat-out ignores the television show on which is was supposed to be based, replacing the fun and camp of the original with a generic and lazily-written actioner.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: It's partly second-rate Bond and partly second-rate Mission Impossible: something to fill the time during the long months before the fall movie season.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E has some flaws, a dash of predictability and some questionable plot turns; but everyone involved brims with how much they're having.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Adopting a deliciously groovy vibe, Guy Ritchie turns the iconic 1960s TV spy series into a flashy action-comedy.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer trade in the same kind of faux-clever one-upsmanship that Holmes and Watson do, with similarly weak dialogue but barely a quarter of the charm.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: I don't know if anyone was clamoring for a movie version of the '60s TV show but it's surprisingly entertaining sandbox for director Guy Ritchie to play in.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: The movie offers nothing new; I think I'll stick with the original TV series. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Solórzano

reviews.text: Long on frothiness and light on plot, this is the swinging 1960s as imagined by people who see it as non-stop fun, punctuated by the threat of nuclear war.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. fulfills its mission to entertain. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Ruiz

reviews.text: It's a brisk, smart, fun action comedy that takes the premise of the 1964-68 TV series, replaces the dated campiness with effortless cool, and dresses it in slick '60s period detail that makes Mad Men look amateurish in comparison.
reviews.author: Gary Dowell

reviews.text: Probably one of the best blockbusters of the year.
reviews.author: Arturo Aguilar

reviews.text: This is a spectacle worth seeing. Ritchie and his team bring the visual vibe of the 1960s in a beautiful way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Paz

reviews.text: This U.N.C.L.E is effortlessly cool.
reviews.author: Reagan Gavin Rasquinha

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E has style to spare, especially when Ritchie matches the richly textured images with perfectly selected music tracks, but substance proves to be more elusive than the nuclear whatsit.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: One actually misses the sizzle that Robert Downey Jr and Jude Law share in the same director's Sherlock Holmes.
reviews.author: Jyoti Sharma Bawa

reviews.text: Great chemistry between its leads and respectable action scenes make this a fun homage to the cold war spy movies. The girls steal the spotlight in this one. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: A good spy movie that doesn't dissapoint. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oswaldo Betancourt Lozano

reviews.text: With great action sequences and unbeleivable chemistry between it's two leads, the movie is everything a spy film should be. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Eduardo Molina

reviews.text: Faithful to the spirit of the original series. A sensational film with an impecable production. Hopefully the beginning of a saga. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Edgardo Reséndiz

reviews.text: Maybe the lowest point on Hollywood's spy fever this year... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gonzalo Lira Galván

reviews.text: An entertainig, over the top movie that never drags too long. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mabel Salinas

reviews.text: A three-quarters full movie, it has all the right components, but it doesn't quite use them in the most effective way.
reviews.author: Amy West

reviews.text: After racing out of the Brandenburg Gate, Ritchie bottles up all the period-flavour with no fizz; there's no real pop here to go along with the cool '60s culture. Not that the story's much more than B-rate bond. After two hours of this, you'll cry uncle.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer barely work up a sweat.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: A straight-forward action film that owes its look to James Bond.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: A slickly executed, hyper stylish mix of action and comedy that seduces by virtue of its visual appeal.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: It's got style and charm, baby, not to mention buckets of liquid eyeliner and an old-fashioned Wartburg car chase.
reviews.author: Janet Smith

reviews.text: This movie, based on the 1960s TV show is slickly done, supported by a solid cast, but the screenplay is a bit muddled. Once it gets free of the opening mire, it works well enough.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's grinning at us the whole time, and for once it feels good to grin right back.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: A deliciously old-fashioned romp brimming with retro chic, and with a champagne cocktail's effervescent fizz.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: ... showcases plenty of visual flair but not much substance beneath the spectacle, turning into a buddy comedy of sorts with little of the sociopolitical texture that the Cold War setting might warrant.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Guy RItchie's in-your-face directorial style serves this blast from the past well but it is the cool and funny chemistry between Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer that makes this a nice tribute to the 60's classic spy series.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: U.N.C.L.E. is much more fun than we expected.
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: The result is a stylishly pleasant surprise, a tongue-in-cheek pastiche of '60s spy movies just as the series itself was a pastiche of the Sean Connery James Bond movies.
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: U.N.C.L.E. has fun playing with Cold War tropes in the decadent playground of 1960s Europe.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: There is certainly some entertainment value to be had here, but a movie that lacks earnestness has a licence to be fun; Ritchie never once properly takes that chance.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: ...bland enough to be received by a global audience, but probably a touch too slick to gain any real purchase on the collective imagination.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Though The Man From U.N.C.L.E. lacks the wit of Kingsman and the spectacle of M:I-Rogue Nation, it nonetheless sits comfortably alongside its spy movie siblings.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. excels at these moments: character-based comedy executed with lightness of touch, capable of extracting laughs without mocking the film's internal realities.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: It's a little calmer than most Guy Ritchie movies, but it's just right for the material. Terrific to look at, brisk, stylish, funny (but just serious enough) and beautifully cast.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Aside from Vikander the period playfulness falls short.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: The superb craftsmanship on display only makes the film's shortcomings more frustrating, though; it's one of the best-looking boring movies ever made.
reviews.author: Jim Hemphill

reviews.text: Despite the fact that it seems to have been designed for a sequel, it's hard to summon up any enthusiasm for the prospect. The characters don't seem to, after all.
reviews.author: Philippa Hawker

reviews.text: Exactly no one was asking for this. So it's a surprise to discover that the bar for this movie is low enough to conga under.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: Super-snazzy and elaborately retro-looking without generating any real excitement, and features irksome stars who seem puzzled as to what the heck's going on.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Slick and stylish, 'The Man From U.N.C.L.E.' isn't quite like the TV series, but it does have a 1960s atmosphere.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Style wins out over substance in Guy Ritchie's playful reimagining of the popular '60s TV show.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: A celebration of the '60s, pop culture and Bond films. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Batlle Caminal

reviews.text: As for Cavill, let us just say that the line between phlegmatic suavity and downright dullness is rather more easily breached than the Berlin Wall.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: A mirthless period spy caper that fails to fulfil Ritchie's stated aim to make espionage movies sexy, fun and frivolous again.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Though overly long, it is an affectionate, uber-stylish and entertaining production that salutes U.N.C.L.E.
reviews.author: Brigit Grant

reviews.text: ('The Man from U.N.C.L.E') is breezy, it's entertaining and it even manages to feel fresh as it treads the most well-worn of territory.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Dressed up to the nines like an expensively retro aftershave ad, Ritchie's film is laboriously insouciant - and no amount of funky drumming and lounge Braziliana on the soundtrack can make it spark.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: A worthwhile endeavor, with Ritchie toning down the spastic shooting style that all but destroyed his Sherlock Holmes films with Robert Downey Jr.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Nothing cerebral but nothing to make you cry uncle either. Fun fluff and the throwback to the 60s is a nice touch. Too bad you never quite believe you're there.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Based on the mid'60s NBC-TV show, it's fashionable, yet forced - and the fun has gone missing.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: There's a stylish charm eagerly at work. Whether that's enough to sustain the equivalent of a James Bond tribute band is debatable, given how wan the rest of the well-meaning enterprise is when it comes to storytelling and starpower.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Funny, stylish and knowingly preposterous, this Sixties-set adventure is just a safari suit away from a Roger Moore era Bond movie.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: It's breezy and elegant - so breezily elegant it can make you laugh out loud from frame to frame.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: While The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is easily one of the best looking films of the year, it seems very similar to dating a supermodel: equally gorgeous and vapid.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: ...the chemistry between bumbling Hammer and Cavill is akin to that between wood and stone...What is Alicia Vikander, the best actress extant, doing in this junk? Her character is little more than a McGuffin. She shouldn't be slumming like this.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: So if you think you'd enjoy some third-rate James-Bondian comic blandness sparkled up by some enjoyable 60s outfits by Joanna Johnston, you just might have a real treat this weekend.
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: Hoping the pounding 60's soundtrack will jar the audience into enjoyment, this yarn evaporates into TV fluff.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: "U.N.C.L.E." must have seemed tailor-made for Ritchie's peculiar talents. (I think I'm going to be using the word "peculiar" a lot when describing this film.)
reviews.author: Burl Burlingame

reviews.text: Like its slick trailer, The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is handsome and inviting, but its rewards are brief and unsatisfying.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: Sleek, seductive and equally dedicated to horseplay and gunplay, The Man From U.N.C.L.E. may not be deep, but its shallowness contains vast pleasures.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: In a quintessential guy flick, Ritchie and co-writer Lionel Wigram have injected some serious girl power.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: This is one of those rare instances when a sequel wouldn't just be warranted - it would be welcomed.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: [They] got it exactly right, introducing the characters to moviegoers who may have never heard of them while not insulting the memories of those who have.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: It proves a perfectly pleasant way of wasting two hours.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: Though viewers will find familiar story beats and characters in The Man from U.N.C.L.E., Ritchie succeeds in creating a fun love-letter to 1960s spy fandom.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's spy-themed GQ fashion shoot. Pure popcorn nonsense, sleek and chic and vaguely funny, but instantly forgettable.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Just in case Tom Cruise and Daniel Craig aren't your cup of super spy tea, The Man from U.N.C.L.E. arrives this weekend on a wave of style that will make you wish it were 1963 all over again.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: While it looks good - Ritchie has always been a slick visual stylist - it's ultimately as passive as an old rerun.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: This clearly isn't a film by or for U.N.C.L.E. nerds and while that's frustrating from the perspective of an overly possessive fan, it's understandable when you remove that bias.
reviews.author: Sarah Kurchak

reviews.text: As a late-summer aperitif - suavely assembled, chilled and tinted by the sunset - this jaunty nonsense slips down smoothly enough.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: An entertaining and refreshingly old-fashioned adaptation of the espionage drama that ran from 1964 to '68 and made stars of Robert Vaughn and David McCallum.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer are great in this, and great together.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: There are hints of a fun, engaging movie here, but I couldn't help but wonder what it would have been like if it was George Clooney's scowl and charm wrapped up in Solo's suit.
reviews.author: Bryan Bishop

reviews.text: Slick and stylized, retro spy adventure is loads of fun.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: 'The Man from U.N.C.L.E' is an ultra-stylish throwback to the spy genre of the sixties and the perfect way to cap off summer.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Fun, but miscast Solo and Kuryakin are a problem. Worth it just for Alicia Vikander's wardrobe.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: If you're looking for two hours of pure adventure and laughs, The Man From U.N.C.L.E. delivers.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: There's still time this summer for another adaptation of a 1960s TV spy series. Generating the same amount of thrills, however, proves to be a true mission impossible.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: There's no weight to any of this stuff, but it has enough fizz that The Man From U.N.C.L.E. doesn't feel derivative.
reviews.author: Scott Renshaw

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. (shouldn't it be Men From U.N.C.L.E.?) is Bond-ish but less violent and it never takes itself seriously.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Henry Cavill is a really, really, really attractive human being.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: There's a rather witty scene with the two heroes arguing over which purse their female accomplice should wear with each outfit, and you think yeah, this could be the entire movie: "The Spy Who Loved To Tell Me What Not To Wear."
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The actors give the impression of having met just moments before the cameras started rolling.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: It's a better catalog than movie, but Man from UNCLE offers enough panache to pacify ticket holders.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: If this is the start of a new franchise, sign me up.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: Has an undeniable entertainment value, so you can enjoy it from scene to scene, but it's not a great movie.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: Mesmerizing and clever, but more style than substance.
reviews.author: Nathalie Atkinson

reviews.text: Even the action is droll - Solo enjoying wine and a sandwich as we see Illya desperately fighting villains in the background, a nice joke that's a small triumph of framing.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Though it's made with lots of modern tricks and technology, it's old-fashioned in the best sense, and not just because it's set in the Sixties.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Calling this (lackluster) movie 'The Man from U.N.C.L.E.' is misleading. Naming it 'The Future Men from U.N.C.L.E.' is probably too cumbersome, but truthful.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: The action is handled well and looks quite stylish, and it's enjoyable being immersed in the trappings of a bygone, Bond-esque espionage era. (Full Content Review - Sex, Nudity, Violence, Profanity, etc. - for Parents available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: ...the sharpest and most literate action film of the summer.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: There are a few spots of humour and one decent chase scene, but The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is essentially a nicely costumed bland-out from one of the most overrated directors of our time.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: It goes down as easy as the cocktails the heroes quaff like clockwork, and while you probably won't remember it in the morning, it won't leave any lingering bad taste.
reviews.author: Rob Vaux

reviews.text: Fans of The Man From U.N.C.L.E. would be advised to skip this revival. Some TV relics were not made for the big screen.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: A slick spy throwback bridging modern sensibilities with '60s-chic reverence.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: The straining pop art production design and heavy-handed genre-blurring only results in a frantic, thrown-together mess.
reviews.author: Alan Jones

reviews.text: Ritchie clearly thinks he's made a classy espionage caper in the same mould as North By Northwest, but he lacks Alfred Hitchcock's understanding of the need to combine humour with suspense.
reviews.author: Toby Young

reviews.text: Cavill and Hammer are made for each other, but the film can't always find the pyrotechnics to match their chemistry.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Hugh Grant is underused as a British intelligence chief but Cavill picks up the slack when it comes to suave comedy. He's way more fun in this movie than as the Man of Steel, and Ritchie's dark sense of humour frequently stops boredom from setting in.
reviews.author: Nick Dent

reviews.text: It's often enjoyable, but it still feels constructed, and if not heartless, then perhaps it's lacking a soul.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's update of the 1960's television spy series is sleek, sophisticated, and sexy, with lively banter, high style, and oodles of roguish retro charm.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: If Bond movies are getting overly serious, Ritchie is intent on seeing that this '60s spy franchise keeps it light.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Maybe this is just glowing praise born out of basement-level low expectations, but I found U.N.C.L.E.'s bouncy vibe to be an utter delight.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: A light spy thriller in the hands of a once "enfant terrible" that has been domesticated.[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: This failed attempt to bring the classic TV show to the big screen fails it's main mission: to entertain [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Arce

reviews.text: The movie finds a perfect balance between not taking itself too seriously and delivering a solid story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: It all winds up feeling hollow and even slightly oppressive, an enforced sense of fun jabbed within quotation marks. It aims for a silky lightness of touch but lands like a dropped slab of concrete.
reviews.author: Mark Olsen

reviews.text: As a summer blockbuster, it's a mod, modest success.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: This smirky reheating of the '60s television series... is much less interested in what it says than in how it looks. And it looks great: the suits, the dresses, the cars, and oh yes, the actors, all in top, mid-century modern form.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Lightweight but stylish and enjoyable in a high-kitsch fashion.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. delivers its spy action in a retro package, with lashings of irony.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: The Cold War returns full force on the big screen, though by the end of The Man from U.N.C.L.E., you might want to put it back in the fridge.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: This film is not about anything other than its own coolness. It is pure post-modern empty pastiche; retrograde fun made for a globalized 21st century.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: "Man" is a celebration of a time when secret agents dressed impeccably, bantered with style, and had exceptionally cool toys. That the movie is almost instantly forgettable is part of the pleasure.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Compared to the latest features in the James Bond franchise or the "Mission Impossible" reboots, "The Man From U.N.C.L.E." is rather quaint.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: It's not going to revolutionize the genre, but there's something fitting about a stylish spy movie that doesn't spend so much time taking itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: What substance it has could be dissolved in a shot glass. But so what?
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: Call me crazy but I'm calling Man From U.N.C.L.E. is some of the most fun you'll have a theatre this summer.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: A lot of energy and effort has gone into this endeavor, and I can't say some of it's not fun. But more of it, alas, is just tedious.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: Not an update of the old TV show but a revival, with dazzling sets, period outfits and wonderfully implausible action. It's an Atomic Age blast.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: This is like an Austin Powers movie directed by Wes Anderson, although Ritchie's personal style is very much in evidence.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: U.N.C.L.E. is maybe turning these spies into idyllic caricatures, but it's not irreverent. Even the bumbling is really cool bumbling.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: While the plot may seem to be of the 'simplicity itself' variety, it is routinely obscured, either intentionally or unintentionally, by Ritchie's stylistic choices.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. plays like a lower key, vintage edition of a Mission: Impossible movie. It's a good movie with a great look.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Ritchie's "U.N.C.L.E" is a bit like a Bond buddy movie with its retro-chic globe-trotting and series of shiny vehicles (including a speedboat and submarine) backgrounding its bumpy bromance.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: As stylish as it is witty, Guy Ritchie's retro spy movie, The Man From U.N.C.L.E., is a lovable lark and full of mischief.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: You want a killer, cutting edge, thoroughly modern The Man From U.N.C.L.E.? This isn't it. But that doesn't mean it isn't bloody good fun.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Ritchie throws buckets of style onto the screen but fails to generate an interesting plot or bring any further dimensions to the characters.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Whose idea was it to make a cold war thriller for a generation that doesn't know what the cold war was?
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. isn't about much, but it made me smile for a while. It's harmless fun.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: No crying U.N.C.L.E. here.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. desperately vies to be Mad Men crossed with Mission: Impossible, but it ends up being a forgettable movie that will be a diverting watch while you're, say, folding laundry or traveling internationally.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: Sexiness and fading nostalgia have powered far worse things than a bubbly, refreshing late-summer spy comedy.
reviews.author: David Berry

reviews.text: As an action director, Ritchie turns out to be off his game, too -- the movie suffers in comparison with the current Mission: Impossible sequel or the similar Kingsman: The Secret Service.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: I thought director Guy Ritchie, who wasn't born when the TV show debuted in 1964, cleverly captures the elements that made it a success ...
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: It's got all the ingredients - improbable romances, partial nudity, ridiculous escapes - that make it little more than big-sound and big-picture fodder for the Imax screens it will appear on throughout the country.
reviews.author: Michael Granberry

reviews.text: Against all odds The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is surprisingly enjoyable.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: It almost works. Actually, it does work, hitting the requisite number of hip notes. It just doesn't dazzle, and that's kind of a surprise.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A misfire on virtually every level...more like 'The Wild Wild West' than 'Mission: Impossible.'
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie makes the kind of enjoyably disreputable movies that are fun to watch until they're not.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It's slow, lethargic, utterly lacking in charm and undeserving of the Cold War setting that is its best trait.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: Henry Cavill, Armie Hammer, Alicia Vikander, Elizabeth Debicki and a delightfully cavalier visual aesthetic return the fun and levity to the spy genre.
reviews.author: Justin Craig

reviews.text: a moldy 1960s TV series that comes to the screen with no Mission: Impossible update or makeover. That's right - it's still moldy. But in a way that's escapist, retro fun.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The threat that this mess of a movie might be followed by a sequel is enough to make anyone cry uncle.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Composer Daniel Pemberton's evocations of early '60s "danger" music respect the period, which is more than can be said for Ritchie's hatchet-style of staging and editing.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Ritchie is a director with no instinct for the audience, and he can't hold things together for an entire film. He seems at a loss, from moment to moment, as to what he should emphasize.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A lot of what it's trying to do is done better in the new "Mission: Impossible" but its music and its female lead make it distinctive.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. feels fun even when it lacks a particular reason for existing.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: This is a movie whose charm sneaks up on you, like a spy in the night.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Superficial charisma and an appealing cast narrowly rescue The Man From U.N.C.L.E. from total collapse.
reviews.author: Sam Woolf

reviews.text: An entertaining homage to retro spy films that makes up for what it lacks in substance with plenty of laughs and undeniable style.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: A remake no one was asking for, but in that category it is more like Ritchie's Sherlock Holmes films - stylishly successful - than Hammer's noisy flop The Lone Ranger.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Henry Cavill won the evolutionary sweepstakes and even without being Ritchie's object of desire, he's the best thing in the movie. Everything else is boring, stunted and a "who cares"?
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Entertaining and admirably low-key. More like a groovy heist thriller than a super spy yarn.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The picture is quite clever and light on its feet.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: Ritchie wants to have it both ways, to make James Bond and "Get Smart." It doesn't work.
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: Feels like a tossed-off piece of work, an instantly forgettable time-killer that's destined to become this decade's The Mod Squad remake.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: "The Man from U.N.C.L.E." often times looks like an ad for a fashion magazine, and there's nothing wrong with that.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: As Ritchie retrofits modern action-comedy tropes onto the Ian Fleming era, he keeps the tone light.
reviews.author: Brian Miller

reviews.text: It would be a mistake to criticize Ritchie's U.N.C.L.E. just because it doesn't faithfully replicate the 1964-68 television series. It shouldn't. But the movie version should at least be as charming and tongue-in-cheek as the low-budget TV spy spoof.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: While The Man From U.N.C.L.E. is definitely the most attractively designed action movie of the year to date, its unabashed good looks aren't enough to stop you noticing your pulse rate isn't exactly rising in a hurry.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: This episode is one of the more enjoyable action experiences this summer. It's certainly the best dressed.
reviews.author: Iain McNally

reviews.text: The movie is fun, if you're content to view it as an exercise in style and fashion.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: The film may be too silly to satisfy action audiences (and a little too slight to get us invested in the stakes), but there's a place for it in a world of self-serious mass entertainment.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: It'll win you over in the first few minutes with an impressively innovative car-chase scene that includes one of the drivers playing dead at the wheel.
reviews.author: Alex Falcone

reviews.text: Cavill's Solo, and the movie, are aggressively quippy, which is what happens when screenwriters set out to be funny but give up when they're halfway there.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: This is not your father's U.N.C.L.E.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: It's certainly brave of Cavill to opt for such an obnoxious characterisation but [how can we] be tense about a potential World War Three when he's more concerned about spilling focaccia crumbs on his tailored three-piece suit?
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Stylish as hell, but missing even the slightest sense of urgency.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Leads Henry Cavill and Armie Hammer do a terrific impression of male mannequins, robbing the picture of needed charm.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Temperamentally, Buy Ritchie aligns more with the lithe, James Bond-like Solo: detached, above-it-all, eternally cool under pressure.
reviews.author: Kenji Fujishima

reviews.text: A stylish, sexy, quintessentially-60s spy thriller that puts 'fun' at the top of its hit list
reviews.author: Matt Looker

reviews.text: A weak, uneasy pastiche of styles and genres in search of a consistent tone.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Nazi fascists, Italian playboys, speedboats, femme fatales, fast cars, double crosses, old-school spy do-daddery and gorgeous, eye-popping fashions. It sometimes looks like the cast of 'Mad Men' left Madison Avenue and went into Euro undercover work.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: For better and for worse, 'U.N.C.L.E.' plays like a super-sized episode - inconsequential, an excuse for smirky fun and the occasional (though too occasional) old school gadget, bound to be repeated, with mild variations, over untold seasons.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: Alicia Vikander, a Swedish actress who plays a German, is more convincing speaking English than Armie Hammer ... a heavy-footed film that barely gets by on one actor's charm.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: If only there were always two Armie Hammers.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: "The Man From U.N.C.L. E." is totally enjoyable for everyone.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: "The Man From U.N.C.L. E." is a dull affair.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Hot people, sexy music, exotic vistas, delicious one-liners - it's everything I always wanted from Bond movies but never got. Finally a spy movie that isn't a joyless slog about an emotional loner.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Fun, it should be noted, is the point of this particular exercise.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: This is a mid-August, end-of-summer, everybody-dial-it-back action movie that requests absolutely nothing from you. Which is sort of fine?
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: Even if it isn't as much of grabber as the TV series, Guy Ritchie's reboot sure gets points for style.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: When will Henry Cavill star in a movie worthy of these newly unveiled charms?
reviews.author: Michael Arbeiter

reviews.text: "The Man From U.N.C.L.E." is only intermittently engaging and amusing, and those portions of the movie that succeed are also frustrating.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: This is an incredibly confident, stylish popcorn movie, full of pleasures large and small.
reviews.author: Jack Giroux

reviews.text: Honors the original characters just fine, but the leads are lukewarm...the [action] mostly unmemorable ...and the split-the-difference jokey-serious tone errs...on the side of fashion-conscious and smug.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: The chemistry between the three leads is magnificent, and the film doesn't run so much as glide through its entirety; taking you, the audience, along for the ride.
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: Long on style but short on substance, Guy Ritchie's ring-a-ding-ding Cold War spy thriller attempts to resurrect a mothballed '60s TV series the way that Mission: Impossible did. It doesn't work this time.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: In the case of Style v. Substance, this retro spy caper finds in favor of Style.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: A pristine Cold War lookbook of 1960s spy fashion.
reviews.author: Karen Krizanovich

reviews.text: Alas, the movie doesn't fulfil the tease of the opening sequence. From there it devolves into a series of revelations with diminishing returns.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: An amusing placeholder for anyone who can't wait for Spectre, the next Bond movie. Which should be everyone, since Skyfall ruled.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Inasmuch as you can leave a movie saying "man, those props, costumes and credits sequences were terrific," you can call The Man From U.N.C.L.E. something of a minor success.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Guy Ritchie's adaptation of the 1960′s television show offers a skewed Daniel Craig/Roger Moore 007 fantasy team-up.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: A passable, nostalgic period piece which does a far better job of recreating Cold War ambience than intrigue.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: While it lacks a memorable villain, and the central pairing fizzes but never sparks, the film gets by on its vintage charm and a third act upswing - and, for all its messiness, it'd be a shame not to see Solo and Kuryakin rutting horns again.
reviews.author: Josh Winning

reviews.text: Ultimately, rising stars Henry Cavill, Armie Hammer and Alicia Vikander are pretty pawns moved around the director's massive retro funhouse, Ritchie endlessly amused by his elaborately empty construction.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: An unusually restrained Guy Ritchie serves up solid entertainment with a classy touch, but bland leads and no-sizzle chemistry make this slick '60s TV adaptation forgettable.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: It's not bad but not quite good enough either.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: You can certainly see why Cavill was in the running to be 007 before donning the red cape of Superman, and why he remains a favourite for Bond once Daniel Craig eventually retires.
reviews.author: Jon Lyus

reviews.text: In the proud tradition of le cinema du Ritchie, The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is yet another film in which its aesthetics are both its greatest virtue and its most ghastly weakness.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: James Bond may have cornered the market in '60s-inpsired spy flicks, but director Guy Ritchie's The Man from UNCLE offers a fizzy antidote to 007's deep psychological probing of late.
reviews.author: Stella Papamichael

reviews.text: U.N.C.L.E. has enough style and smarts to make it an amusingly louche summer movie: a cultivated mix of action and wit, suits and cities.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: With brisk pacing, and a cast this attractive parading the kinds of fashions that will remind you how much you miss Mad Men, most of the movie boasts a Mod crispness.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Leaves you in a place where you'll be dying to see more of these characters.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

synopsis: At the height of the Cold War, a mysterious criminal organization plans to use nuclear weapons and technology to upset the fragile balance of power between the United States and Soviet Union. CIA agent Napoleon Solo (Henry Cavill) and KGB agent Illya Kuryakin (Armie Hammer) are forced to put aside their hostilities and work together to stop the evildoers in their tracks. The duo's only lead is the daughter of a missing German scientist, whom they must find soon to prevent a global catastrophe.
